o1.biggest_strength: It uses the ad data to force taste-first openings, answers the $3-a-can objection directly, and gives the team production, disclosure and test rules they can act on tomorrow.
o1.biggest_mistake: The plan says every script answers '$3 a can' on camera, but only Script 2 does; Scripts 1 and 3 show $35.99 but not the per-can price or a spoken price answer.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the $3/can price answer explicit in every script, or stop claiming it is, and trim the extra rules so the team gets one tight page plus the three scripts.

o2.biggest_strength: The scripts are clean, natural and easy to shoot, with hooks taken from customer language and creator briefs that give the right amount of freedom.
o2.biggest_mistake: Script 3's alternate hook changes the whole scene, so it cannot be tested as a first-3-seconds-only hook; the test plan also has no clear budget or decision thresholds.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add specific test budgets and cut/scale thresholds, keep every alternate hook to a true first-3-second change, and include spoken disclosure plus delivery and rights details.

reason: Output 1 is the one I would hand to my team: it is more data-led, more complete on disclosure and production, and gives clearer test decisions. Output 2 is cleaner and has strong creator briefs, but it is less specific on testing and has a hook-test setup that does not fully hold together.
